input.question: Let M be a sigma-compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold of dimension n > 0, let p be a point of M, and let Diff_c(M)_{p,0} be the subgroup of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms fixing p whose tangent map at p has positive determinant. Is every formal diffeomorphism of R^n whose linear part has positive determinant realized as the Taylor series at p of some element of Diff_c(M)_{p,0}? Equivalently, is the Taylor-series homomorphism T_p^infinity: Diff_c(M)_{p,0} -> G^n_f(R)_0 surjective?

rewritten_question: Let M be a sigma-compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold of positive dimension n, let p be a point of M, and let Diff_c(M)_{p,0} be the group of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms of M that fix p and whose derivative at p has positive determinant. Choose a local chart around p that sends p to 0 in R^n. For γ in Diff_c(M)_{p,0}, let T_p^infinity(γ) be the full Taylor series at 0 of the local representative of γ in that chart. If G_f^n(R)_0 denotes the group of formal diffeomorphisms of R^n whose linear part has positive determinant, must every element of G_f^n(R)_0 occur as T_p^infinity(γ) for some γ in Diff_c(M)_{p,0}? Equivalently, is the Taylor-series homomorphism T_p^infinity: Diff_c(M)_{p,0} -> G_f^n(R)_0 surjective?

resolution.status_reason: The cited paper itself states this surjectivity theorem in the introduction and proves it in Section 4 by reducing to M = R^n and invoking Lemma 4.2, which constructs a compactly supported smooth diffeomorphism with any prescribed formal Taylor series whose linear part has positive determinant. A bounded Crossref search identified the journal publication of the same work; no separate later solving paper was needed because the cited paper already contains the proof.

paper_evidence.quote: Moreover, we prove a result by the author announced in [21], which answers a question posed in an earlier, unpublished version of the survey.

Borel’s Theorem for Diffeomorphisms. Let a finite-dimensional smooth manifold M of dimension n be given, p ∈ M and φ be a local chart around p such that φ(p) = 0. For each γ ∈ Diffc(M), let T∞p(γ) denote the Taylor series of φ ◦ γ ◦ φ−1 around 0. Then T∞p : Diffc(M)p,0 → Gfn(R)0 is a surjective homomorphism of Lie groups.

Lemma 4.2 Let n ∈ N and aα ∈ Rn for multi-indices α ∈ Nn0 be given such that A := (ae1, . . . , aen) ∈ GLn(R) and det(A) > 0. Then there exists φ ∈ Diffc(Rn) such that (∂αφ)(0)/α! = aα for each α ∈ Nn0.
In this case, the surjectivity of T∞p : Diffc(Rn)p,0 → Gfn(R)0 has been established in Lemma 4.2. The Chain Rule for Taylor Polynomials entails that T∞p is a homomorphism of groups.
